prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly JSON-decodes string arguments for parameters whose annotation is a union containing str (e.g. `str | None`), corrupting legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1]") because the original check only special-cased annotation being exactly `str`, not str-containing unions. prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2032's _should_pre_parse_json compares union args by exact membership in a frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; it never unwraps Annotated, so the very common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern (idiomatic for described optional params) still fails the check and keeps pre-parsing/corrupting those values — the bug persists for that case. PR #2032 also widens the skip to any union of 'simple types' (e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool`), which changes behavior for those unions: since pydantic won't coerce a bare numeric/boolean string to int/bool in a union with str, skipping pre-parse there can prevent previously-working JSON-encoded int/bool values from being converted at all. PR #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparing, so it correctly handles the Annotated-wrapped case, and scopes the fix narrowly to `str | None` (the reported failure mode), avoiding the broader behavior change to other primitive unions.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2032's _should_pre_parse_json compares union args by exact membership in a frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; it never unwraps Annotated, so the very common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern (idiomatic for described optional params) still fails the check and keeps pre-parsing/corrupting those values — the bug persists for that case. PR #2032 also widens the skip to any union of 'simple types' (e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool`), which changes behavior for those unions: since pydantic won't coerce a bare numeric/boolean string to int/bool in a union with str, skipping pre-parse there can prevent previously-working JSON-encoded int/bool values from being converted at all. PR #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparing, so it correctly handles the Annotated-wrapped case, and scopes the fix narrowly to `str | None` (the reported failure mode), avoiding the broader behavior change to other primitive unions.

Previously `cancel()` sent a bogus error response via `respond()` to indicate cancellation, which is non-compliant with the JSON-RPC/MCP spec (a cancelled request must not receive a normal response). #2493 removes that erroneous response-send and correspondingly updates the duplicate-suppression comment in server.py. #2514 makes the same underlying edit but goes further: it imports `CancelledNotificationParams` and has `cancel()` emit a proper `notifications/cancelled` message, covering both request-timeout and caller-initiated cancellation, and it removes a `# pragma: no cover` marker from the adjacent guard clause, indicating a new test now exercises that branch. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a 409/400-style rejection for duplicate in-flight request ids on the same `_request_streams` map, but #3221 fixes an edge case #3063 leaves open: #3063 keys the map with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id "1" into the same key (a false-positive 'in flight' rejection) and doesn't guard against a string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel ("_GET_stream"). #3221 introduces a type-preserving key (`_request_stream_key`, prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and explicitly documents why it can't collide with `GET_STREAM_KEY`, making it the more complete fix for the same underlying race.

PR #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparing, so it correctly handles the Annotated-wrapped case, and scopes the fix narrowly to `str | None` (the reported failure mode), avoiding the broader behavior change to other primitive unions.
